title: Ops reliability collab: stakeholder roadmap and sprint slate
summary: Working plan to align product, SRE, platform, and CS on a 10-week sprint slate that converts high-level SLO commitments into implementable telemetry, rollout, and contingency artifacts. Focus: pragmatic SLOs, predictable error-budget handling, and clear cross-team handoffs for upcoming model-serving launches.
objectives: 1) Reach cross-functional agreement on a small set of service-level objectives for the model-serving surface by end of week 2. 2) Produce telemetry + alerting config for each SLO (weeks 2-5). 3) Create error-budget policies, escalation and fallback runbooks (weeks 4-8). 4) Validate SLOs with a canary launch and tabletop exercises (weeks 8-10).
scope: In-scope: hosted API endpoints, dedicated inference pools routing layer, and model-variant fallback logic. Out-of-scope: billing model changes, long-term capacity procurement (>90 days), and deep model quality evaluations (those live in applied-ml evals).
deliverables:
- SLO definitions (latency P95/P99, availability, tail-QPS guardrails) as a short spec.
- Telemetry mapping (metrics, logs, traces) and alert thresholds.
- Error budget policy doc and automated burn tracking dashboards.
- Canary runbook and rollback checklist.
- Stakeholder RACI and onboarding checklist for feature teams.
timeline:
Week 0: Kickoff + stakeholder alignment workshop (product, sres, infra, console, cs).
Week 1: Draft SLO variants and service boundary mapping.
Week 2: Finalize SLOs and publish short spec; schedule telemetry owners.
Week 3-5: Implement telemetry + dashboards; iterate alerts.
Week 4: Draft error-budget policy and incident playbook.
Week 6: Tabletop for high-impact failures; update playbook.
Week 7: Canary plan verification and dry run.
Week 8: Live canary (limited traffic), monitor burn.
Week 9: Post-canary retro + adjustments, sign-off for full rollout.
Note: timeline assumes two-week sprint cadence with asynchronous workstreams for telemetry and ops automation.
milestones:
M1: Stakeholder commitment to SLOs (end week 2).
M2: Telemetry coverage >= 90% of SLO signals (end week 5).
M3: Error budget automation in dashboards (end week 6).
M4: Canary executed and rollback tested (end week 8).
M5: Formal handoff to oncall and product owners with acceptance sign-off (end week 10).
roles_and_responsibilities:
- Platform-Engineering (owner): runbook templates, routing policy changes, canary orchestration.
- SRE (co-owner): validate alerts, define recovery SLOs, run tabletop.
- Product/Feature team: agree SLO targets, provide traffic profiles, run user-impact assessment.
- Console + Observability: build dashboards, expose burn metrics in Console.
- Solutions/CS: rehearse customer communication and post-incident messaging.
Primary contacts: Morgan Patel (platform), Sofia Ruiz (SRE), Liam O'Connor (product), Diego Martinez (console).
slo-negotiation-playbook:
Step 1: Surface three candidate SLOs per service (latency, availability, correctness proxy).
Step 2: Share traffic and failure-mode data to ground expectations.
Step 3: Use error-budget language: conservative, exploratory, permissive tiers.
Step 4: Agree on rollback thresholds and automatic fallback policies.
Step 5: Attach acceptance tests mapped to SLOs for deployment gating.
telemetry-mapping: For each SLO define: metric name, aggregation window, source (ingest layer / model-serving), owner, dashboard. Example: latency_p95_ms (1m window) -> serving-gw -> owner: Diego Martinez. Alert on sustained window crossing >2x expected for 3 windows. Include synthetic checks for user-facing latencies.
error_budget_policy:
- Budget: define monthly error budget per SLO.
- Burn detection: automated with two-tier alerts: early-warning (30% burn) and urgent (60% burn).
- Actions: at early-warning: pause non-essential experiments; at urgent: trigger incident bridge and rollback plan.
- Governance: product and SRE must approve any budget consumption plan.
- Communication cadence: weekly burn snapshot to execs while in-risk; daily when urgent.
canary_and_rollout:
Canary approach: traffic-shift with staged percentages (1%, 5%, 25%, 100) over 6–24 hours depending on traffic.
Rollback triggers: SLO metric crossing urgent threshold OR anomalous model-quality regression signal.
Rollback checklist: pre-approved rollback command, owner contact list, runbook step for data collection, post-rollback retrospective owners.
tabletop_exercise_plan:
Simulated scenarios: 1) sudden P99 spike, 2) regional outage causing 40% capacity loss, 3) model fallback producing elevated low-confidence responses.
Participants: SRE, platform, product, console, solutions.
Output: updated runbook lines, new alerts, and prioritized tech debt to prevent repeat failures.
communication_plan:
- Weekly sync (30m) during sprint window; invite product and feature leads.
- Burn alerts to #ops-burn Slack channel with automated dashboard link.
- Incident-level notifications to PagerDuty and leadership paging list.
- Customer-facing status templates owned by Solutions team; prewritten for common failure modes.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: mis-specified SLOs that either overcommit or are irrelevant. Mitigation: require data-backed targets and a 30-day probation period.
Risk: telemetry gaps. Mitigation: early instrumentation sprint and synthetic checks.
Risk: cross-team delays. Mitigation: enforce RACI and weekly escalation to EMs.
Risk: canary causes customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: limit initial traffic and have automatic circuit-breakers.
acceptance_criteria:
- SLO spec signed by product, SRE, and platform.
- Dashboards show live burn with automated alerts.
- Canary executed without urgent error-budget triggers, or if triggered, rollback validated and retro completed.
- Runbooks published and linked in Console with owners assigned.
next_steps:
1) Schedule kickoff workshop (owner: Morgan) and book the 2-hour slot.
2) Product teams to supply traffic slices and expected SLAs by EOD week 1.
3) Console owners to stand up initial dashboard template (pending PR link).
4) SRE to draft tabletop scenarios and invite participants.
5) Platform to prepare canary gating automation and rollback playbook.
notes_to_self: Keep SLO list deliberately short (3–5 per service). Avoid mixing model quality SLOs with infra SLOs in the same spec — keep cross-references instead. Track disagreements in JIRA and escalate weekly.
related_documents: See linked artifacts and recommend merging final SLOs into the canonical reliability governance page after sign-off.
